http://www.euronews.com/2026/08/26/nepal.text: Over 380 tourists, mostly foreigners, were out of contact in Nepal on Wednesday after a massive flood tore through the border region with Tibet."A preliminary agency-wise record received from tourism and travel companies has identified 384 travellers, including 291 foreign nationals and 93 Nepali nationals, who were reported missing from the affected areas," said Nepal Tourism Board, noting authorities were working to verify the travellers' whereabouts."Nineteen bodies have been recovered so far. We are intensely coordinating the rescue and relief efforts. Many in our police force are also out of contact," Nepali police spokesperson Abi Narayan Kafle said.Videos shared by Nepal police and others on social media showed torrents of muddy water crashing through mountain valleys in the Himalayan district bordering China."I witnessed the flood sweep away eight or nine trucks, along with houses and people," Suman Chalise, a 34-year-old teacher, told AFP in Nuwakot district."It was absolutely heart-wrenching. I had not witnessed such devastation before."The police spokesperson said earlier that authorities did not know the extent of the damage but said they had "alerted people who are staying near the riverside to relocate."The Nepal Army said it had deployed helicopters and disaster response personnel to the affected area.The Nepal Electricity Authority said about 430 megawatts of production capacity, including from hydropower and solar facilities, has been damaged."The disaster has damaged the production, transmission and distribution facilities of the Authority...resulting in disruption of electricity supply," it said.Sarthak Shrestha, a remote sensing and geo information analyst at the Kathmandu-based International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD), said a preliminary assessment showed "no anomalies" from China's side of the border."We believe a rock-ice avalanche occurred in Nepal, blocking the Lhende river and causing the cascading flood event," he said.Mudslide riskSeveral highways were also closed, Nepali authorities said.Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported on Wednesday that "a mudslide disaster on the Nepalese side resulted in major casualties and missing people at the Gyirong Port" in Tibet.Footage shared by the broadcaster, showed rushing water carrying tree branches and debris, as well as a flooded road.State news agency Xinhua said Chinese President Xi Jinping had urged "all-out" rescue operations, but did not provide figures on injuries or deaths.Xi said that "the most urgent task is doing everything possible to search for and rescue the missing people...quickly treat injured people and minimise casualties to the greatest extent possible," according to CCTV.Traffic authorities in Tibet's Shigatse said roads in the area were "at risk of mudslides and unsafe for passage" in a post on social media on Wednesday.In July last year, 17 people went missing after a mudslide near the Gyirong Port, Xinhua reported at the time.Monsoon rains from June to September regularly trigger deadly floods and landslides across South Asia.

https://www.mfa.gov.lv/en/article/eu-for.text: EU Foreign Affairs Council adopts largest-ever package of sanctions listings against Russia Published: 12.10.2026. Flickr Photo: European Union Facebook X / Twitter Linkedin Threads On 12 October 2026, Minister of Foreign Affairs Baiba Braže attended a meeting of the European Union (EU) Foreign Affairs Council, at which the largest-ever package of individual sanctions against Russia was adopted. The Minister called for continued pressure on the aggressor state, including a ban on the transit of Russian grain at the EU level. Baiba Braže met with Andrii Sybiha, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine, expressing support for Ukraine, and briefed her colleagues on the situation at the Latvian–Belarusian border, emphasising the need to strengthen the security of the EU’s and NATO’s external borders. During the meeting, the EU’s most extensive package of individual sanctions to date against Russia was approved, covering 1,569 individuals and entities, including individuals and companies linked to Russia’s military-industrial complex. The ministers also adopted sanctions against 77 individuals involved in organising the illegal Russian State Duma elections held in temporarily occupied Ukrainian territories. During the EU Foreign Affairs Council meeting in Luxembourg, Baiba Braže also met with Andrii Sybiha, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine, who expressed his immense gratitude to Latvia for its comprehensive support for Ukraine. The Minister emphasised the need to significantly increase all forms of support for Ukraine, including military, financial, energy and humanitarian aid, ahead of the coming winter. Baiba Braže reiterated her call to EU Member States to agree on a ban on Russian grain imports and transit across the entire EU. During the discussion on Russia’s war of aggression in Ukraine, Baiba Braže drew attention to the civilian casualties caused by Russian attacks – last week, more than 100 people were killed and hundreds injured. The Minister stressed the need to increase military support for Ukraine, particularly in air defence, and to strengthen the resilience of Ukraine’s energy infrastructure against Russian attacks. Baiba Braže briefed the ministers on the situation at the Latvian–Belarusian border, highlighting the recent escalation. The Minister reported that several deliberate provocations had been recorded the previous week. In one incident, armed and masked individuals directed at least 20 migrants towards the Latvian border and threatened Latvian soldiers. In another incident, masked individuals cut through the border fence, entered Latvian territory, damaged the power supply infrastructure and stole surveillance cameras. “This is not just Latvia’s border – it is the external border of the EU and NATO,” the Minister emphasised, calling for increased pressure on Belarus and Russia. Latvia has already prevented around 12,000 illegal attempts to cross the border this year. Discussing EU enlargement, Baiba Braže emphasised that it represents a strategic investment in Europe’s security. Latvia supports the opening of all accession negotiation clusters with Ukraine and Moldova before the end of this year. At the same time, candidate countries must fully align themselves with the EU’s common foreign policy and its sanctions against Russia and Belarus. Ministers also discussed the situation in the Middle East, including regional security challenges, the situation in Gaza and the West Bank, and cooperation with the Gulf states. Latvia reaffirmed its support for diplomatic solutions, regional stability and a two-state solution to the Israeli–Palestinian conflict.
